summary.headline: Radico Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 1,684 crore and EBITDA Rs 348 crore (20.7% margin, record); P&A volumes up 36%.
summary.overview: Radico reported record quarterly IMFL volume of 10 million cases (up 3% YoY), revenue of Rs 1,684 crore and EBITDA of Rs 348 crore. Premium and above (P&A) volumes grew 36%, while regular volumes declined on a higher base after the Andhra Pradesh route-to-market change and policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Gross margin rose 610 bps YoY to 49.1% and EBITDA margin rose 536 bps YoY to 20.7%. Management reiterated about 20% EBITDA margin for FY27 and raised P&A volume growth guidance to over 25% from 20%, and said it is on track to become net debt free by Q2 FY27.

segments.name: P&A (Prestige & Above)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 36% in Q1; FY27 guidance raised to over 25% volume growth from 20%. Flavored vodka is 75% of Magic Moments volume, up from 65%.

segments.name: Magic Moments (vodka)
segments.commentary: 3.25 million cases, +43% YoY, over 60% category share; vodka share of Indian IMFL rose from 4.6% in Q1 FY26 to 6.1% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Luxury portfolio
segments.commentary: FY26 luxury turnover about Rs 475 crore; management says it is on target for 25% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Non-IMFL
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin about 11% to 11.5% in Q1, versus 6% to 7% in the recent inflationary period; management calls this sustainable.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Brands sold in over 100 countries; exports are about 5% to 6% of volume, with a higher share of value; 63 global travel retail outlets and 50 to 63 airports (target 100).

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin of around 20% for FY27, with management saying it sees room for pluses and minuses.
P&A volume growth over 25% in FY27, raised from 20%; management does not give quarterly guidance.
Luxury portfolio sales value growth of 25% in FY27.
Maintenance capex of Rs 150 crore to Rs 170 crore; the rest of surplus cash to be decided by the Board.
Net debt free by Q2 FY27; minimum dividend payout policy of 20%.
Gross margin expansion trajectory expected to continue in FY27, despite West Asia-related packing material volatility (about Rs 30 crore impact in Q1).
capex_capacity: ENA requirement is about 28 to 30 crore litres (IMFL and non-IMFL); own capacity across Rampur, Sitapur and the JV is about 33 crore litres.
No plans for new ENA capacity expansion; outsourced ENA for mass brands is available and most states are ENA surplus.
Maintenance capex Rs 150 to 170 crore; management said acquisitions are unlikely and growth will stay organic.
Airport presence raised to 63 from 50 (target 100); on-trade expansion described as ahead of the 1,000-events plan.
demand_pricing: Karnataka premium brand pricing rationalised; P&A category grew 9% in Q1 while Radico's P&A grew 83%; effect of new MRPs expected from July.
Maharashtra MML: industry down about 20% in Q1 after a 35% fall last year; Radico has about 7% to 8% share in MML (6 to 7 lakh cases) and P&A grew about 10% there.
UK FTA: management estimates retail prices could fall only 7% to 8% if competitors pass on the benefit; says Radico's single malts are priced above competition.
Price increase in Q1 FY27 contributed about 75 bps to margin.
Tamil Nadu market opening is a watch item; management says Morpheus brandy is performing well in premium brandy.
Morpheus whisky launched in 10 to 12 states; early traction but still in seeding phase.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained at 20% EBITDA and how does ENA cost exposure matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 20% EBITDA margin for FY27 and said more clarity will come later in the year. Mix shift to P&A is expected to support margins, reducing ENA sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20.7% margin sustainable, and what are IMFL and non-IMFL margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-IMFL margin is about 11% to 11.5% and IMFL is 23%+. Non-IMFL margins historically ranged 8% to 11%, fell to 6% to 7% during inflation, and management considers current levels sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan once debt free?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex is Rs 150 to 170 crore; the remainder is for the Board to decide. Acquisitions only if they make sense for shareholders; management says Radico has always grown organically and sees no brand acquisition opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Magic Moments 43% growth a trade-loading one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied trade loading, citing strong credit control, and said the growth is tertiary-driven, with month-on-month traction continuing.

qa_highlights.question: How will the India-UK FTA affect pricing and competition in luxury?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to comment. Management says single malt is taste-driven, and retail prices may fall only 7% to 8% if passed on; no pricing changes planned yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will A&P spend increase given P&A growth well ahead of peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Ad spend has been held at 7% to 8% of sales; management says spend is focused on direct marketing, in-shop and digital, and that P&A has outpaced the industry for 10 years.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and West Asia-related supply chain volatility, including packing material cost (about Rs 30 crore impact in Q1).
ENA cost increase could pressure margins; ENA captive requirement exceeds captive capacity in some periods and is supplemented by outsourcing.
Regular volume decline (Andhra Pradesh route change, Maharashtra and Karnataka policy) and falling royalty volumes.
Competitive intensity in vodka and luxury from new entrants; India-UK FTA could reduce imported single malt prices.
Tamil Nadu market opening and Bihar prohibition as potential upside.
Sustainability of 43% Magic Moments growth and the implied slower 22% growth needed for the rest of FY27 to meet the 25% target.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on premiumisation, P&A momentum and margins, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to give quarterly guidance and called the UK FTA impact too early to assess. Answers on ENA capacity and Tamil Nadu were framed as wait-and-watch.
key_quotes: During Q1 FY 27, we reported highest ever quarterly volume of 10 million cases, revenue of Rs. 1,684 crores and EBITDA of Rs. 348 crores.
Magic Moments continues to lead the category with over 60% market share and an even stronger position in its core price segment.
We don't give quarter-on-quarter guidance, we give annual guidance, which we already have done where we have increased the yearly guidance from 20% to 25%.
So, I think it's a multiyear story for vodka.

adds.what: Airport presence raised to 63 outlets from 50 (target 100); no capex figure given

growth.why: P&A volume growth guidance raised to over 25% for FY27 (from 20%) and luxury sales value growth of 25% held, backed by Magic Moments +43% volume and a 63-airport footprint, but no new capacity or order book is specified and EBITDA margin is guided only at around 20%.
